gaps.requirement: Section 1 Q2, Q3 and section 2B items 4-5 (P0): 'Works with' (formats, dimensionality, important limitations) and 'Produces' (masks, tracks, tables, plots, reports) directly under the one-sentence summary; section 4: inputs, outputs, limitations as the principal new scientific fields, enforced for analysis apps, living in the app repository.
gaps.current: None of the six pages has a Works with, Produces or Limitations block, and the schema has no field for them (schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json properties: only name, summary, description, quickstart, kind, hosts, distribution, authors, license, categories, doi, homepage, docs_url, icon, screenshots). The page order in pages_apps.py:189-207 is header, Get it, About, screenshots, Using it, All downloads, Details. The facts exist but only as README prose: CellTracksColab README 'Required File Format' table (CSV or XML; CSV) and 'does not yet support track merging or splitting'; NucleiSky README 'Two Golden Rules' (pixel size in um/px must be correct; segmentation quality) plus docs/limitations.md and docs/exports.md; GuessTheCondition README 'Prepare your images' (.tif/.tiff, folder per condition and repeat) and its results list; Playground 'Honest limits'. A visitor deciding whether NucleiSky accepts their OME-Zarr or whether CellTracksColab accepts CellProfiler output has to open GitHub, which is exactly what the central principle forbids. Verified with a scratch copy of the schema (appaudit/schematest.py): adding optional inputs, outputs, limitations, example_data keeps all six current manifests valid, while the current schema rejects a manifest that uses them ('Additional properties are not allowed').
gaps.proposal: Add three optional arrays to the manifest schema: `inputs`, `outputs`, `limitations` (1-6 plain-text items, each 5-160 characters; the length cap keeps it a summary, not a README copy). Render a 'Works with' and a 'Produces' block between the header and 'Get it', and a 'Limitations' list under 'Using it'. When a field is absent show 'Not stated by the author' (visible, not omitted) and add one WARNING per app to catalogue.resolve's `warnings` list that names the missing fields (apps in the testing section and kinds game/training exempt for inputs/outputs). Warnings never unlist an app, matching the icon-warning precedent (catalogue.py:82). Fill the six seed/manifests drafts from the READMEs for the preview; the real values go in each app's own labconstrictor-app.yaml. Rollout order matters because additionalProperties is false: publish the site schema first, then the initialiser and the apps. Put the new rendering in a new module (pages_apps.py is 208 of 300 lines, page_app must stay at or under 30 lines) with tests for present, absent and over-length cases.
gaps.rule_conflicts: No conflict with AGENTS.md or the author-controlled principle: the author writes the text, it lives in the app repository, the site only fetches it, and an absent field is shown as 'Not stated' plus a warning instead of a silent default (read with `in` or optional_list, not .get with a default). DESIGN.md has no pattern for the block, so add it there first, in the same change. Needs matching changes in LabConstrictor_streamlit (schemas/ copy, app_manifest.py, manifest_form.py) and the template's app-manifest guide (.tools/docs); not done by this site alone. Risk to watch: authors pasting README paragraphs would create the 'second description' the rules forbid, hence the length cap and docs_url for the rest.
